related_content.name: Lachlan Giles and Ariel Tabak Guard Retention System
related_content.relationship: Use the passing-route organization when a forced guard change repeatedly becomes a pass.

summary: A topic guide for recognizing changes between open guards and distinguishing a deliberate switch from a passer-forced change.
description: Use a public positional glossary to describe guard changes precisely before selecting a specialized guard guide.
overview: Open guard covers many configurations, not one fixed position. This guide uses Kesting and Bayev’s terminology to make observation notes more precise: record what changed and why before calling every movement a transition system.

fits: You recognize individual guards but struggle to describe the moment one becomes another.
consider_alternative_if: If the recurring problem is a specific passing route, use the Giles–Tabak retention guide for a more focused study map.

includes: The glossary distinguishes open from closed guard and explains that changes can be chosen by the bottom player or forced by the passer.
Named open-guard examples provide a vocabulary for comparing contacts.
limits: This is an observation framework, not an instructor-authored curriculum called Dynamic Guard or a rule to keep moving constantly.

start_here.title: Describe one guard change without guessing a chain
start_here.task: Read the open-guard introduction on printed page 9. In one exchange you can review, name the guard before and after the change. Mark whether the bottom player initiated it or the passer forced it. If the configuration is unclear, describe the visible contacts instead of assigning a name.

sources.note: Inspected the introduction and open-guard section on printed pages 3 and 9–14: terminology, changing guard positions and examples. This is a positional reference, not a demonstrated training sequence.

sources.note: Verified both instructors and parts devoted to around-the-legs, north-south and under-the-legs retention; scope follows title and detailed outline. Listing inspected; course video content not reviewed.

flashcards.question: Must every change from closed guard to open guard be voluntary?
flashcards.answer: No. Kesting and Bayev distinguish a deliberate opening from one forced by the opponent while passing.
flashcards.answer_line: It can be deliberate or forced.
